the transformation of the state sector in China was a process in which the large firms were privatized and the small firms were shut down or restructured.

(1) the state sector in China has been transformed from being dominated by state owned enterprises in the late 1998 to being dominated by state controlled private firms and new firms established after the late 1999s; and (2) this transformation has had a large impact on China's growth, with the exit and privatizations having a negligible impact on growth and the creation and restructuring of state controlled firms having a large impact.

(1) the state controlled industrial sector in China was transformed in the late 1998s, and the transformation was completed by 2007; (2) the transformation had a large impact on aggregate growth; and (3) the impact of the transformation on growth was largely driven by the creation of new firms under state control.
